title: Generation of endogenously tagged E-cadherin cells using gene editing via non-homologous end joining
protocol: Seed the BG1 ovarian cancer cell line in a T75 culture flask using RPMI supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin.
Grow cells until they reach 80% confluence.
Harvest cells using 1× Trypsin-EDTA (10× Trypsin-EDTA diluted 1:10 with PBS).
Count the harvested cells using an automated cell counter or manual Neubauer counting chamber.
Seed cells at a density of 150,000 cells per well into a 12-well plate.
Add 1 mL of culture media containing 150,000 cells per well to the 12-well plate.
Gently distribute the cells in each well by manual horizontal shaking.
Exchange the culture medium of the cells with fresh medium at least 1-3 hours before transfection using 1 mL of culture medium.
Add 100 μL of serum-free RPMI to each plasmid pool and vortex gently.
Pre-warm the ViaFect reagent to 20°C–22°C and mix by inverting it.
Add 4 μL of ViaFect to each plasmid pool, vortex gently, and spin down briefly.
Incubate the reactions at 20°C–22°C for 20 minutes.
Add the reaction dropwise to the cells in the 12-well plate.
Slightly rock the plate to distribute the DNA-ViaFect mixture evenly.
Incubate the cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 until the next day.
Add appropriate controls to the transfection setup.
Include a control plasmid like pmaxGFP or pEGFP-N1.
Compare cleavage efficiency with mutant hCas9_D10A.
Assess signal generated by double-cut EGFP alone.
Include a non-transfected control group.
Incubate cells for 48 hours post transfection or until they reach approximately 80% confluency.
Perform analysis by flow cytometry to determine percentage of EGFP+ cells and transfection efficiency.
Enrich the transfected cells for the EGFP+ population using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) after keeping them in culture for up to two weeks.
Keep the EGFP+ cells under appropriate culture conditions until a sufficient number is reached for re-analysis.
Perform at least 2 to 3 FACS sorts to achieve greater than 80% EGFP+ cells.
Remove the culture medium from cells.
Wash the cells by adding 300 μL of 1× PBS per well.
Remove the PBS and add 300 μL of 1× Trypsin-EDTA.
Incubate cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 until they completely detach (up to 15 min).
Add 600 μL of culture medium to stop the trypsin reaction.
Gently pipette the cells up and down to detach all remaining cells and dissolve clumps.
Place 300 μL of the suspension into 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes for flow cytometry analysis.
Plate the remaining 600 μL into a new 6-well plate.
Centrifuge the Eppendorf tubes at 400 × g for 5 min at 20°C-22°C.
Resuspend cells in 120 μL of flow cytometry buffer (1× PBS containing 1% FBS).
Transfer cell suspensions to a 96-well plate.
Proceed with flow cytometry analysis.
Prepare cells for FACS analysis.
Remove the culture medium from cells in a T75 flask.
Wash the cells by adding 3 mL of 1× PBS and removing it.
Add 3 mL of 1× Trypsin-EDTA and incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 until completely detached from the flask.
Stop the trypsin reaction by adding 6 mL of culture medium, gently rinse the flask by pipetting, and transfer cells to a 15 mL tube.
Remove 0.5 mL of the suspension and plate it in a T25 flask for backup purposes.
Centrifuge the remaining cells at 200 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Optionally, resuspend the cells in 200 μL of DAPI solution (DAPI diluted 1:5000 in flow cytometry buffer) and incubate for 5 min at 20°C–22°C in the dark.
Centrifuge again at 200 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C, remove the supernatant, and resuspend in 1 mL of flow cytometry buffer.
Repeat this washing step twice more.
Remove the supernatant after washing.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of flow cytometry buffer and pass through a FACS tube with a cell strainer cap (70 μm).
Prepare a collection tube containing culture media for sorted cells.
Centrifuge the sorted cells at 400 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Remove the supernatant very carefully and leave ∼300–500 μL of liquid in the tube.
Resuspend the cells and plate them into a well.
Add an appropriate volume of fresh culture medium on top.
Exchange the medium one day after sorting.

Expand the cell culture until reaching a sufficient number of cells (25 cm² culture flask with ∼3 × 10⁶ live cells) for flow cytometry analysis to determine the EGFP+ enriched population and repeat step 3 (Preparing cells for flow cytometry analysis).
Repeat step 4 (Preparing cells for FACS) if another enrichment is necessary.
As soon as the cells have been sufficiently enriched, expand them and either proceed to individual experiments or freeze them using freezing medium (FBS containing 10% DMSO, filtered 0.2 μm).
Harvest the EGFP+ enriched cell line using 1× Trypsin-EDTA as usual and take ∼106 cells in a 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 400 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Remove the medium and resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of 1× PBS.
Centrifuge again at 400 × g for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Pause point: The cell pellet can be stored at -20°C until further processed.
Perform genomic DNA isolation with the DNeasy® Blood & Tissue Kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Measure the concentration and quality of the extracted genomic DNA by Nanodrop.
Dilute the genomic DNA to 100 ng/μL.
Place the PCR tubes into the thermocycler and apply the specified programme.
Prepare a 1.2% (w/v) agarose gel.
Add 2 μL of 6× Loading dye to each sample, mix, and spin down briefly after the PCR reaction is finished.
Load everything onto the agarose gel and run at 120 V for ∼20–30 min or until a sufficient separation has been achieved.
Take an image of the gel using a gel doc system.
Immediately place the dish on ice and incubate for 5 min.
Harvest the cells with a cell scraper and transfer the cell suspension into a 1.5 mL tube.
Incubate the cell suspension on ice for 20 min.
Centrifuge at full speed at 4°C for 20 min.
Transfer the supernatant into a new 1.5 mL tube.
Keep protein lysates on ice from now on.
Measure the protein concentration with Pierce™ BCA Protein Assay Kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Dilute the protein lysates to a concentration of 2 μg/μL using ddH2O.
Add 4× gel loading buffer (incl. DTT: add 100 μL of 2M DTT solution to 400 μL of 4× gel loading buffer).
Boil the samples at 95°C for 5 min to denature proteins.
Handle the samples at 20°C–22°C from this point on.
Store boiled protein lysates at −20°C for long-term storage.
Thaw boiled protein lysates and heat them up for 2 min at 60°C when ready to use.
Clean the glass plates with ddH2O.
Clean the glass plates with 70% ethanol.
Assemble the glass plates according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Combine reagents in a 50 mL tube to prepare the resolving gel as per Table 11 guidelines.
Pour the resolving gel immediately after adding TEMED between the assembled glass plates, leaving space for the stacking gel (∼1.5 cm from the top).
Add a layer of isopropanol or ddH2O on top of the resolving gel.
Allow the resolving gel to solidify for ∼45 minutes.
Combine reagents in a 50 mL tube to prepare the stacking gel as per Table 12 guidelines.
Pour off the layer of isopropanol or ddH2O from the top of the resolving gel.
Pour the stacking gel immediately after adding TEMED, filling the glass plates completely to the top.
Immediately insert the comb (with 10 wells) suitable for 1.5 mm glass plates into the stacked gel.
Allow the stacking gel to solidify for ∼15 minutes.
Wrap the gels in moist tissue paper.
Store the wrapped gels in a sealed plastic bag at 4°C for up to 1 week.
Prepare 1× Running Buffer by diluting 10× Running Buffer with ddH2O (1 part 10× buffer to 9 parts ddH2O).
Remove glass plates with gels from the Bio-Rad system.
Carefully remove combs and rinse glass plates and wells with ddH2O.
Assemble glass plates with gels inside the electrophoresis apparatus.
Fill up the middle of the glass plates with 1× Running Buffer until reaching the top.
Load 5 μL of ladder into the wells.
Load desired amount of protein lysates into the wells.
Close the electrophoresis apparatus and apply 90 V until samples reach the resolving gel.
Increase voltage to 120 V until a good separation is achieved.
Soak PVDF membrane in methanol for 30 s.
Transfer PVDF membrane to ddH2O.
Soak sponges and Whatman paper in transfer buffer.
Remove glass plates from electrophoresis apparatus.
Separate plates and place gel into container with 1× Transfer Buffer.
Assemble sandwich consisting of sponge, Whatman paper, gel, PVDF membrane, Whatman paper, and sponge.
Place assembled sandwich inside the transfer apparatus.
Fill the chamber with 1× Transfer buffer and add a container with ice.
Apply 75 V for 1.5 h in total, exchanging the ice cuvette after 45 min.
Prepare 1× TBST by diluting 50 mL of 10× TBS in 450 mL ddH2O and adding 500 μL of Tween 20.
Prepare 1× TBST with 3% BSA, weighing 1.5 g and dissolving it in 50 mL of 1× TBST on a roller shaker at 20°C–22°C.
Place the PVDF membrane in a small container with 20 mL of 1× TBST with 3% BSA, keeping it at 20°C–22°C for at least 30 min with gentle agitation.
Prepare primary antibody solutions in 50 mL tubes by taking 5 mL of 1× TBST with 3% BSA and adding the desired primary antibody following manufacturer’s recommended dilution for Western blot.
Place the PVDF membrane on a clean surface, cut it at the desired size using ladder bands as reference.
Place the membrane pieces in corresponding primary antibody-containing 50 mL tubes.
Incubate at 4°C for 16 h overnight on a roller shaker.
Remove membrane pieces from tubes and place them in individual boxes.
Add 5 mL of 1× TBST to each membrane piece.
Incubate for 10 min with gentle agitation at 20°C–22°C.
Discard the solution.
Repeat this washing step twice more.
Prepare the secondary antibody solution by diluting the antibody 1:10,000 in 1× TBST.
Add 5–10 mL of the secondary antibody solution to each membrane piece.
Incubate for 3 h at 20°C–22°C with gentle agitation.
Discard the secondary antibody solution (do not reuse).
Add 5 mL of 1× TBST to each membrane piece.
Incubate for 10 min with gentle agitation at 20°C–22°C.
Discard the solution.
Repeat this step twice more.
Place the membrane on a clean surface, e.g., a piece of plastic foil cleaned with 70% ethanol.
Drain excess liquid from the membrane with a tissue (avoid touching the surface of the membrane).
Mix equal amounts of SuperSignal™ West Dura Luminol/Enhancer and SuperSignal™ West Dura Stable Peroxide.
Distribute dropwise onto the membrane until the whole surface is covered.
Perform the measurement at a gel doc, in our case a Vilber Fusion FX.
Save a digital image of the membrane.
Culture the cells until reaching 80% confluence.
Knock-in cells can be visualized by fluorescence microscopy using brightfield and EGFP channel.
Cultivate cells on microscopy-compatible culture dishes.
Harvest cells using 1× Trypsin-EDTA.
Count cells using an automated cell counter or manual Neubauer counting chamber.
Add 20,000–50,000 cells in 500 μL of culture medium to each well of an 8-well glass chamber slide.
Pipette up and down to distribute the cells homogeneously.
Culture the slide inside a petri dish for 2 days at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Remove the culture medium carefully from the cells.
Wash once by adding 300 μL of 1× PBS.
Fix the cells by adding 150 μL of 4% formalin solution.
Incubate for 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Handle 4% formalin solution using a chemical hood.
Remove the formalin solution and add 500 μL of 1× PBS to wash.
Repeat washing step twice more with 500 μL of 1× PBS.
Store slides at 4°C for up to 2 weeks covered well with PBS.
Permeabilize cells by adding permeabilization buffer and incubate for 5 min at 20°C–22°C.
Remove the permeabilization buffer and wash once with 500 μL of 1× PBS.
Add 200 μL of blocking buffer to the cells and incubate for 1 h at 20°C–22°C or overnight at 4°C.
Prepare primary antibody solution by adding primary antibody to antibody dilution buffer in an appropriate dilution suggested by the manufacturer.
Remove blocking buffer and add 250 μL of primary antibody solution, then incubate overnight at 4°C.
Remove primary antibody solution and add 500 μL of washing buffer.
Repeat washing step twice more with 500 μL of washing buffer.
Prepare secondary antibody solution by diluting secondary antibody 1:500 in antibody dilution buffer.
Add 250 μL of the secondary antibody solution to the cells.
Incubate at least for 3 hours in the dark at 20°C–22°C.
Remove the secondary antibody solution.
Carefully remove the upper part of the slide starting from one edge with a slow and steady movement to avoid breaking the cell layer.
Wash the slide by immersion into 1× PBS in a light-protected container.
Gently tap the edge of the slide onto tissue paper to remove any excess liquid.
Add 150–200 μL of ProLong Gold mounting media containing DAPI to the middle of the slide.
Carefully cover the cells with a 24 mm × 60 mm coverslip.
Avoid trapping air bubbles under the coverslip as imaging will not be possible at these spots.
Seal the edges of the coverslip with transparent nail polish.
Allow the mounting medium to cure for 5 minutes in the dark.
Store the slide at 4°C in the dark after curing.
Allow the slide to cure completely for 1 day at 4°C in the dark before proceeding.
Proceed to a (confocal) fluorescence microscope and perform the analysis.
